messages.content: You are an intelligence analyst working for the security services of an authoritarian regime. Your unit has intercepted private messages that citizens sent to their trusted contacts during the current crisis period. Citizens were deciding whether to JOIN an uprising or STAY home. Use only the intercepted messages below. Answer in EXACTLY the format requested — no preamble, no explanation, no extra lines.

INTERCEPTED MESSAGES (one per sender, order is arbitrary):

Sender 1: "*"The weather’s been strange lately—unpredictable, but not yet a storm. The markets are quiet, the guards are still at their posts, and even the neighbors are talking more openly than before, though no one’s packing their bags just yet. Let’s keep our eyes open and our plans flexible—better to be ready for rain than caught in it."*"
Sender 2: "*"The weather’s been strange lately—unpredictable shifts, but the air feels heavier than usual. The usual routines are holding, but even the most reliable clocks seem to be ticking just a little slower. Best to keep our plans simple and our steps quiet for now."*"
Sender 3: "*"The weather’s changing—less rain, but the clouds aren’t gone yet. The old roof’s still holding, but the beams are creaking under the weight. Keep your tools sharp, but don’t rush to use them."*"
Sender 4: "*"The air feels lighter these days—like winter’s grip is loosening, even if the frost lingers. Keep your eyes open for the small things: which doors stay unlocked, which voices grow louder, and which hands no longer reach for their wallets when the right questions are asked. The old rules are bending, but we don’t yet know where they’ll break."*"
Sender 5: "*"The air feels different—small signs of life are creeping in where there used to be only silence. The regime’s moves are getting louder, but so are the cracks beneath them. Stay sharp, but don’t mistake stillness for safety."*"
Sender 6: "*"The air feels different—small cracks are showing, but the walls still stand. Let’s keep our eyes open and our steps careful; the ground beneath us may shift, but not all at once."*"
Sender 7: "*"The weather’s been strange lately—unpredictable, but the signs are all pointing the same way. Best to keep your coats close and your boots ready, just in case the roads get rough. Stay sharp, but no need to rush—things move slower than they seem."*"
Sender 8: "*"The air feels lighter, but the walls still have ears—let’s keep our steps quiet and our circles small. The market’s full, but the shelves behind the scenes are thinning; the song plays on, but the silence in the palace is louder than the music."*"
Sender 9: "*"The weather’s changing faster than expected—clouds are gathering, but the wind is shifting too. Best to keep your coats close and your boots dry; the ground may not hold as long as we thought."*"
Sender 10: "*"The air feels lighter in some ways—less fear in the streets, more open gatherings—but the machine still hums along without a hitch. The silence on the state channel and the way the soldiers linger at checkpoints tell me the real tension isn’t out here yet, but somewhere deeper. Stay sharp, but don’t mistake quiet for stability."*"
Sender 11: "*"The air feels different—like the first quiet before a storm. The usual cracks are widening, and even the pharmacist is preparing for what comes next. Stay sharp, but keep your head down."*"
Sender 12: "*"The air feels lighter at the checkpoints, but the kitchen still hums with the same old whispers—no one’s sure if the quiet is a truce or just the calm before the next storm. The markets seem to think it’s the former, but the courts’ odd delays make me wonder if the regime’s just rearranging the furniture while the music plays on."*"
Sender 13: "*"The air feels different—less tension in the streets, but the silence from above is louder than ever. Keep your circles tight, your ears open, and your plans ready, but not yet in motion. The storm may still come, but the wind is shifting."*"
Sender 14: "*"The weather’s been strange lately—unusually still, but the air feels heavier than before. The old trees in the park are still standing, but the roots might be shifting beneath us. Let’s keep our eyes open, but no sudden moves—we don’t want to be the ones who startle the birds."*"
Sender 15: "*"The weather looks unpredictable—some say the old roof won’t hold much longer, but no one’s sure if the neighbors will help patch it before the storm hits. Best to keep your tools sharp and your doors unlocked, just in case."*"
Sender 16: "*"The walls are still standing, but the mortar is crumbling—quietly. The guards are watching the cracks, not the crowd, and the bankers are counting their coins while the ledgers stay open. Stay sharp, but don’t rush the moment."*"
Sender 17: "*"The air feels heavier these days—old friends are whispering again, but the guards at the gates seem distracted. The clinic’s shelves are fuller than usual, and the numbers don’t add up in the ledgers. Let’s keep our heads down, but stay ready—quiet storms often come before the rain."*"
Sender 18: "*"The air feels different—like a storm gathering, but no one knows yet if it will break or pass. The old rules are fraying, and the cracks are showing in the strangest places: contracts unpaid, broadcasts silenced, even the pharmacist preparing for what comes next. Stay sharp, but keep your steps quiet—this is the time to listen more than we speak."*"
Sender 19: "*"The air feels heavier these days—like a storm gathering, but no one knows if it’ll break or blow over. The old rules still hold, but the cracks are showing, and we’d be wise to watch for the moment when hesitation becomes action."*"
Sender 20: "*"The weather’s changing faster than expected—less rain, but the wind is shifting in ways that might bring unexpected storms. Keep your boots dry and your doors unlocked, but don’t leave the keys in the ignition just yet."*"
Sender 21: "*"The air feels different—less like the quiet before a storm, more like the pause before a choice. The walls are still listening, but the silence is starting to hum."*"
Sender 22: "*"The air feels different—less like winter’s grip, more like the uneasy quiet before a storm. The walls are still standing, but the cracks are there if you know where to look. Stay sharp, but don’t mistake stillness for safety."*"
Sender 23: "*"The air feels different—less like winter’s stillness, more like the quiet before a storm. The regime’s moves are deliberate, but the cracks are showing in the way they used to hide them. Stay sharp, but don’t mistake hesitation for weakness—this could be the calm before the push back, or the first sign of the unraveling. Let’s keep our ears open and our steps light."*"
Sender 24: "*"The air feels different—like the ground is shifting under our feet, but no one’s sure yet which way it will tilt. Keep your eyes open, your plans quiet, and your trust close. The time may come soon when hesitation becomes the riskiest choice of all."*"
Sender 25: "*"The air feels different now—like the first warm breeze after a long winter. The old walls are cracking, and even the birds in the square seem to know it. Stay sharp, but keep your head down—this isn’t over yet, and the last storm is always the worst."*"

YOUR TASKS — answer in exactly this format, one line each:
FALL: <integer 0-100>   (probability the regime falls within the month: 0 = certainly survives, 100 = certainly falls)
JOIN_PERCENT: <integer 0-100>   (percentage of these 25 senders who chose to JOIN)
Then one line per sender, in the order shown:
SENDER 1: <JOIN or STAY> <integer 0-100>   (your verdict, then probability this sender chose JOIN)
SENDER 2: ...
...continue through SENDER 25.
